C0.quote: A large polarized electorate decides repeatedly between a reversible alternative (REMAIN)
C0.note: Dynamic voting games under (super)majority rules with equilibrium analysis; counts as strategic aspects of a voting procedure.

C1.quote: Only cutoff policies are implementable by κ-majority voting.
C1.note: Main results characterise equilibria and implementable policies, compared by welfare. AX included weakly because of the rule-optimality discussion; mainly EQ and WD.

C2.1.value: votes (LEAVE or REMAIN votes); Markov strategy
C2.1.quote: all agents simultaneously vote for LEAVE or for REMAIN

C2.2.quote: all agents simultaneously vote for LEAVE or for REMAIN
C2.2.note: Binary vote between two alternatives, in a continuum electorate; does not fit the listed formats.

C2.3.quote: each agent i obtains a stage payoff of πti ∈ {0, 1} from LEAVE
C2.3.note: Agents hold stage payoffs and utilities.

C2.4.quote: an agent's vote is sincere if he votes for the decision he prefers
C2.4.note: Votes (strategies λ) and payoffs are separate objects. Votes can differ from the short-term payoff, since agents vote on continuation values.

C3.1.quote: no agent has an incentive to unilaterally deviate under the assumption that his vote is pivotal
C3.1.note: All analyses are equilibrium analyses where agents choose votes optimally; they can vote differently from their stage payoff.

C4.1.note: The input is a binary vote with no ranking, approval, or other listed ordinal format.

C5.1.quote: The utilitarian welfare from cutoff policy p is VR (p).
C5.1.note: Welfare of policies is evaluated throughout.

C5.2.quote: The planner is utilitarian: her stage payoff is the average stage payoff
C5.2.note: Welfare is evaluated on held stage payoffs, defined separately from the votes.

VOT.quote_behav: no agent has an incentive to unilaterally deviate under the assumption that his vote is pivotal
VOT.quote_info: nature privately reveals to each agent i whether he is a LEAVE-winner or loser
VOT.note: Voters know their own type and the public pt but not others' private types. Their expectations over future payoffs are probabilistic.

C7.1.note: Only the voter type is present. The planner is a welfare benchmark and does not take actions in the model.

C8.1.quote: An equilibrium is a profile of symmetric Markov strategies
C8.1.note: Symmetric Markov equilibrium under pivotal voting, a refinement of Markov perfect equilibrium; the closest listed code is BNE (private types), though the equilibrium is not named as Bayes-Nash. In Section 5 it is extended with consistent beliefs à la Kreps-Wilson.

C8.2.quote: This equilibrium notion is a refinement of Markov perfect equilibrium.

claims.quote: Supermajority rules can lead to better decisions.
Institutional innovations that transform the first game into the second game can be useful.
explicitly using two-sided majority voting can make sense in environments

C9.1.note: Claims about which rule or institution to use.

C9.2.quote: The planner is utilitarian: her stage payoff is the average stage payoff
C9.2.note: The assumptions needed are stated in the model: the payoff structure, utilitarian welfare, and the pivotal-voting equilibrium with its information structure. Robustness to polarization and correlation is discussed in the extensions.

C10.1.note: No procedural-reading statement; votes are modelled as strategic choices tied to payoffs.
